226:class MaskMap:
227:    """
228:    A general utility class that encapsulates the way the bitmask/listofvalue idiom
229:    works in X protocol. It understands a special attribute _maskvalue on
230:    objects, which will be used instead of the object value if present.
231:    This lets us pass in a Font object, rather than Font.fid, for example.
232:    """
233:
234:    def __init__(self, obj):
235:        self.mmap = []
236:        for i in dir(obj):
237:            if not i.startswith("_"):
238:                self.mmap.append((getattr(obj, i), i.lower()))
239:        self.mmap.sort()
240:
241:    def __call__(self, **kwargs):
242:        """
243:        kwargs: keys should be in the mmap name set
244:
245:        Returns a (mask, values) tuple.
246:        """
247:        mask = 0
248:        values = []
249:        for m, s in self.mmap:
250:            if s in kwargs:
251:                val = kwargs.get(s)
252:                if val is not None:
253:                    mask |= m
254:                    values.append(getattr(val, "_maskvalue", val))
255:                del kwargs[s]
256:        if kwargs:
257:            raise ValueError(f"Unknown mask names: {list(kwargs.keys())}")
258:        return mask, values
